Therefore, objection raised by the Registry is over ruled.

Heard on I.A.No.23285/2024, second application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C/corresponding Section 430 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to applicant.
It is revision, therefore, provision of Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C and Section 430 of BNSS are not applicable.
However, said default is ignored subject to payment of cost of Rs.10000/- in the M.P. High Court Bar Association Fund.

sentences.text: Heard on bail application.

Applicant was convicted for commission of offence under Sections 7(i) & 7(iii) read with Section 16(1)(A)(i) Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 by the learned JMFC, Khandwa (M.P.) vide judgment dated 03.11.2017 passed in RCT/800174/2011 (State of M.P. Vs. Daulat Singh).

sentences.text: The aforesaid judgment was assailed by filing an appeal, but the same was dismissed and the judgment passed by the learned JMFC, Khandwa was affirmed vide appeal judgment dated 02.11.2022 passed in 2 CRR-4402-2022 Cr.A.No.199/2017 (Daulat Singh Vs. State of M.P.)

entities.text: Daulat Singh Vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been erroneously convicted by both the Courts below as they have not taken into consideration the fact that on the date on which the offence alleged to have been committed Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was not in force, the same has already been repealed by Food Safety Standard Act, 2006.
Therefore, it was not justified for the Courts below to convict the applicant under the provisions of the repealed Act.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the applicant is 78 years old man and on account of old age related infirmities and problems it has become difficult for him to survive.
Therefore, it is prayed that the jail sentence of applicant may be suspended and he may be released on bail, till final hearing in revision.
On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State has opposed grant of bail and suspension of jail sentence.
In this revision, legality, propriety and correctness of the judgment passed by the Courts below has been assailed.
Simultaneously, it is also contended that the provisions of the Act, under which the applicant has been convicted were also not in force on the date of alleged commission of offence.
As such a serious question for determination arises.
This is a new revision and there is a bleak possibility of hearing of this case in near future,
Applicant is old and infirm person.

Therefore,
having taken into consideration the submissions putforth by the learned counsel for the appellant, I find it a fit case for suspension of jail sentence of the applicant.
Hence, I.A.No.23285/2024 is allowed.

It is directed that execution of jail sentence of applicant Daulat Singh shall remain suspended during pendency of this revision petition and he be released on bail subject to depositing entire fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on 05.12.2024 and on all subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in that regard.
List this revision for final hearing in due course.
